objective: Deliver the complete Elixir language server vision with independent source intelligence and optional BEAM enrichment.

phases.name: Completion, refactors, templates, and agent controls

completion_policy.instructions: Continue through all ready tasks. Record concrete blockers and complete unaffected work.

tasks.title: Verify the shipped scaffold
acceptance: The pinned Rust toolchain and Python versions are recorded.
All Rust tests and the external protocol smoke pass in the harness environment.
The report names absent Elixir, OTP, or OMP tools without a substitute pass.
The feature matrix matches actual advertised capabilities.
The baseline benchmark remains labeled scaffold evidence.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Create independent acceptance runners
acceptance: Every catalog case has a stable source anchor and an explicit oracle.
Supported exact cases and expected refusals have separate denominators.
The runner fails on a missing expected target or an extra incorrect target.
Compiler oracle tests use a real toolchain and retain its identity.
Unavailable oracle environments produce a blocked result, never a pass.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Harden transport and lifecycle
acceptance: Frame limits apply before allocation and malformed headers have deterministic behavior.
Initialization, shutdown, exit, duplicate requests, and unknown methods follow the protocol contract.
Only framed protocol data appears on stdout.
Request cancellation and client disconnect release resources.
Fuzzed or fragmented frames cannot panic or cause unbounded allocation.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Implement a versioned document store
acceptance: Full and incremental changes preserve the exact client text.
UTF-16, UTF-8, CRLF, combining characters, and non-BMP positions pass independent tests.
Obsolete versions never replace a current document.
Invalid edits leave the prior document intact and expose the failure.
Open overlays retain precedence over disk text until the defined close transition.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Model projects and worktree identity
acceptance: Plain source folders, Mix projects, umbrella roots, and workspace folders have explicit identity.
Two worktrees with different source or dependencies never share mutable state.
Symlink aliases do not duplicate one logical file or collapse different worktrees.
Case-sensitive and case-insensitive path behavior is tested on the relevant platforms.
A project scan excludes generated build trees and respects explicit include and exclude settings.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Reconcile external file events
acceptance: OMP-style disk writes become visible through a tested synchronization path.
Open overlay precedence survives concurrent disk writes.
Create, delete, rename, atomic replacement, and watcher overflow trigger correct invalidation.
The implementation recovers from missed events through a bounded reconciliation mechanism.
A watcher never recursively indexes its own cache or build output.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Implement incremental syntax updates
acceptance: Accepted changes update the prior tree through correct Tree-sitter edit coordinates.
Malformed edits preserve useful source structure with bounded work.
Quoted code, comments, and strings do not create false active declarations.
Instrumentation records changed bytes and parse work for repeated body edits.
A parser or grammar upgrade invalidates incompatible persisted syntax data.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Build the source declaration index
acceptance: Document and workspace symbols work without Mix or a PLT.
First useful file results do not wait for a complete workspace scan.
Incremental updates replace only affected file entries.
Deletes and renames remove stale entries.
Index readiness and coverage remain explicit during a partial initial scan.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Persist and invalidate source caches
acceptance: Cache keys include schema, grammar, project identity, configuration, and relevant content identity.
Atomic writes and corruption recovery preserve service availability.
A stale cache never overrides current open text.
Worktree and dependency changes invalidate the correct scope.
Unrelated source files retain reusable data after a small edit.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Add a bounded incremental query scheduler
acceptance: Semantic queries use explicit inputs and coherent immutable snapshots.
The Salsa choice or equivalent design has a recorded compatibility and latency comparison.
Cancellation removes obsolete work before it overwrites newer results.
Worker tasks cannot starve source requests.
Instrumentation proves selective invalidation after function-body edits.
Queues and concurrent jobs have bounded resource limits.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Resolve modules and lexical scopes
acceptance: Nested modules, aliases, imports, and requires follow documented scope rules.
Import only and except constraints produce exact supported targets.
Variables with the same name in different scopes remain distinct.
Quoted declarations remain inactive unless verified enrichment establishes their origin.
Ambiguous runtime module values produce explicit unsupported behavior.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Resolve callable identity and arity
acceptance: Function identity includes module and arity.
Defaults, pipe calls, captures, guards, and multi-clause functions resolve correctly.
Private functions never resolve as public remote exports.
Supported delegates preserve both declaration and delegated target relationships.
Operator-named functions and supported special forms have dedicated fixtures.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Implement exact definitions and references
acceptance: Every supported positive fixture returns the complete expected target set.
Comments, strings, and same-spelling unrelated symbols do not create references.
Source requests succeed during a deliberately stalled compiler worker.
Locations use the negotiated position encoding.
Incomplete reference domains never produce a falsely complete empty array.
Range changes after external edits retain correct source identity.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Expose source documentation and signatures
acceptance: Hover links source declarations with their documentation and typespec facts.
Declared specs remain distinct from inferred or Dialyzer-derived facts.
Signature help handles active arguments and supported pipe or capture forms.
Missing documentation does not become invented documentation.
All source ranges and fallback behavior have independent fixtures.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Add implementations and call hierarchy
acceptance: Protocols and supported defimpl targets have explicit identities.
Behaviours and callback implementations resolve within the documented domain.
Call hierarchy includes only statically resolved calls.
Dynamic calls remain outside complete call-graph claims.
Workspace symbols support bounded, cancellable queries during index updates.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Supervise an optional project worker
acceptance: Source-only mode starts no Elixir, Erlang, Mix, or Dialyzer process.
Enriched mode discovers an explicit supported Elixir and OTP pair.
The manager and worker use the versioned local protocol.
Worker startup, failure, cancellation, and restart have bounded deadlines.
The manager labels unsupported runtime pairs and preserves source mode.
The process boundary is not described as an OS sandbox.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Coalesce project compilation
acceptance: Repeated save events coalesce without an unbounded compile queue.
The worker uses isolated project build artifacts with correct runtime and dependency keys.
It never fetches dependencies automatically or launches the application server.
A failed build preserves source index availability.
Small edits do not force full dependency rebuilds.
Compiler jobs identify their input revision and cannot overwrite newer state.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Import compiler and macro metadata
acceptance: Exports, docs, callbacks, and specs come from the supported compiler or BEAM metadata.
Generated functions retain provenance and a valid source relationship when available.
Project modules cannot collide with worker infrastructure modules.
Macro changes invalidate the appropriate enriched facts.
Source facts remain available when expansion fails or times out.
The implementation does not claim static parity for arbitrary macro execution.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Merge and version diagnostics
acceptance: Syntax and compiler diagnostics retain separate provenance and freshness.
Obsolete compiler diagnostics never replace newer source diagnostics.
Push versions and pull result IDs follow negotiated client capabilities.
A failed build or unavailable worker never reports a clean successful compile.
Cross-file invalidation handles deleted and renamed files.
Diagnostic waits remain independent from ordinary source navigation.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Complete contextual completion and semantic tokens
acceptance: Local variables, aliases, imports, modules, members, and callbacks use the resolver.
CompletionList.isIncomplete is accurate when more analysis can change the result.
Text edits use valid ranges and compatible document revisions.
Source completions remain available without enrichment.
Generated members appear only when verified metadata supports them.
Semantic tokens classify supported syntax and resolved identities through a stable advertised legend.
Token ranges use the negotiated encoding and never overlap or exceed the source document.
Full token results belong to one document revision. Delta support requires separate equivalent-result tests.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Implement conservative rename
acceptance: Local rename requires complete current lexical scope evidence.
Project rename requires complete supported reference coverage.
Open-document edits carry source versions, and client acceptance tests reject mismatched versions.
Preview changes exactly the expected symbols and no comments or unrelated identifiers.
Ambiguous macro or dynamic references produce a specific refusal.
Default-arity groups and multi-clause functions preserve identity.
Closed-file and mixed edits require an explicit client content-hash precondition contract or a strict refusal.
Cross-file acceptance tests cover intervening disk edits and the documented limits of client transaction support.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Add formatting and safe code actions
acceptance: Formatting uses the current document snapshot and the explicit formatter configuration.
Formatter execution has a deadline and never blocks source navigation.
Code actions have exact before-and-after fixtures.
Code actions retain their source preconditions, and client acceptance tests reject obsolete edits.
Only verified action kinds appear in capabilities.
Standard formatting TextEdit arrays remain unversioned. Strict automatic application requires a verified client content-hash check.
Code-action and formatting tests include concurrent open-document changes and external disk edits.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Add explicit optional deep analysis
acceptance: Dialyzer runs only after an explicit configured job request.
PLT identity includes the required runtime and dependency facts.
An ordinary source edit never forces a full PLT build as a query prerequisite.
Canceled and failed jobs retain honest status and bounded resource use.
No deep-analysis result changes declared typespec facts into inferred guarantees.
This optional feature remains independently disabled by default.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Support structural features and template source mapping
acceptance: Dedicated template syntax and embedded Elixir mappings preserve exact positions.
Unicode and multiline template fixtures pass definition and diagnostic tests.
Unsupported framework-specific expansion has explicit behavior.
Template extensions appear in the client configuration only after their gates pass.
Template edits do not invalidate unrelated Elixir modules.
Selection ranges form ordered parent ranges that contain the requested position and remain within document bounds.
Folding ranges match Elixir and template syntax, respect client range limits, and recover after malformed edits.
Structural feature fixtures cover UTF-8, UTF-16, CRLF, empty files, and nested constructs.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Expose negotiated agent analysis controls
acceptance: Versioned status distinguishes source index, worker, and diagnostic states.
Optional batch requests use one coherent snapshot and bounded output.
The source synchronization barrier reconciles external edits under the documented ownership rule.
Standard Location and reference arrays contain no invented completeness fields.
Unsupported custom protocol versions fail explicitly without breaking standard LSP.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Complete configuration and operations
acceptance: Every documented setting maps to implemented behavior and a validation test.
Default logs omit source text and secrets.
Cache recovery affects only the selected Quicksilver project cache.
Worker and source failures have actionable status and bounded recovery.
Configuration reload preserves project identity and document ownership.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Verify the actual OMP workflow
acceptance: The report identifies the installed OMP version and effective LSP configuration.
The evaluated project selects Quicksilver and explicitly disables both elixirls and expert.
The client launches a prebuilt binary rather than cargo run.
Definitions and references remain useful through rapid disk edits and a stalled worker.
Single-file and workspace diagnostics have honest observed behavior.
The adapter preserves semantic errors and freshness instead of converting them to success.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Execute semantic and runtime coverage
acceptance: Every mandatory catalog case executes with its declared oracle.
Exact supported cases achieve all expected targets without false positives.
Refusal cases remain separate from supported correctness counts.
Supported Elixir and OTP pairs execute real compiler fixtures.
The final feature matrix includes every tested capability and deliberate limitation.
A coverage matrix maps every mandatory SEM and PRO behavior to executed evidence or an explicit release blocker.
The corpus expands beyond the seed with direct variable, alias, and import hygiene cases and pinned real project cases.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Measure production latency and invalidation
acceptance: Small, medium, and large corpora have reproducible manifests.
Cold, warm, worker-active, and repeated-edit scenarios retain raw samples.
All required percentile budgets pass or remain explicit release blockers.
Failures, timeouts, and unattempted work remain in the denominator report.
Measurements identify hardware, source revision, binary hash, and cache state.
Instrumentation proves that body edits do not repeatedly rebuild all dependencies or the PLT.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Prove recovery and resource bounds
acceptance: At least 10000 edit cycles preserve freshness and stable resource behavior.
Worker crashes and compile failures do not kill the source service.
Memory and process counts remain within the documented acceptance bounds.
Cache corruption and watcher overflow recover through tested paths.
Canceled requests and client disconnects leave no orphan worker.
The test covers repeated worktree switches and dependency changes.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Build and verify release packages
acceptance: Linux x86_64 and macOS arm64 execute the supported source feature suite.
Unexecuted platforms remain experimental rather than supported.
Release archives install and run from clean directories.
Source archives include lockfiles, licenses, and reproducible verification commands.
Checksums and dependency inventory accompany each candidate package.
No registry or external release is published without owner authorization.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.

tasks.title: Complete independent release review
acceptance: An independent reviewer verifies requirements against code and evidence.
Every required task has current passing acceptance evidence.
The final report states capability coverage and deliberate limitations.
The final report includes semantic, latency, resource, OMP, and platform evidence.
No unavailable gate is reported as a pass.
The release validator passes without weakened acceptance conditions.

verify.additional_requirement: Execute task-specific acceptance tests and preserve the exact commands and results in the evidence report.
